question.text: Ms. Ananya Ghosh's Cat II AIF 'Sahyadri Capital' invested USD 2 million in preference shares of 'Priya Robotics' for a 15% stake with a 2.0x Participating Liquidation Preference. The startup is acquired for USD 40 million. What does Sahyadri Capital receive?

answer.text: USD 9.40 million (USD 4 million preference PLUS 15% of remaining USD 36 million)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Managers workbook on liquidation preference (pp. 294-295), Participating Liquidation Preference gives the investor BOTH the preference multiple and pro-rata participation in the remaining proceeds. Step 1: 2.0x preference on USD 2 million invested equals USD 4.00 million paid first. Step 2: Remaining proceeds equal USD 40 million minus USD 4 million, that is USD 36 million. Step 3: Sahyadri's 15 percent pro-rata share of the USD 36 million remainder equals USD 5.40 million. Step 4: Total received equals USD 4.00 million plus USD 5.40 million, that is USD 9.40 million. The Trap: USD 6 million is the plain pro-rata conversion outcome without any preference. USD 4 million is the 2x preference only, as if the investor did not also participate in the remainder. USD 2 million is simple return of capital with no preference at all. Note: Under a participating preference, the investor does not have to elect between the preference and the pro-rata conversion; both apply, as described on pp. 294-295 of the source.
